page.layout: Running head at top centre, page number 40 at top left. Two circular portrait medallions side by side at the head of the text, each with legend lettering; no printed text beside them. One text column below, in full width, with no margin notes.

main_text.p: NICOSTRATA, Euandri Archadis mater,futurorum vaticinatrix fuit,quę à carminibus,quibus Phoebi oracula enū-tiabat,Carmentis latinè dicta fuit. Hanc quidam aiunt latinis primùm literas dedisse. Diony.Halicarnafeus lib. quidè 1. Antiq.Rom.scribit ipsos Archades primos literas in Italiam attulisse,qui post Pelasgos venerant. Tit.Liuius Euandrum ipsum, autorem vocat,lib. ab vrbe condita 1. Euāder(inquit)tum ea,profugus ex Peloponnefo,autoritate magis quàm imperio regebat loca,venerabilis vir miraculo literarū,rei nouæ inter rudes artium homines. Huic concinit Cornelius Tacitus,qui tradit Aborigenes ab Euādro Archade didicisse literas. Vide Poly. Verg.li.1.cap.6. Hāc quoque scribit Textor Græcas literas impensè doctam, plerasque ex latinis primùm reperisse: quò coniectare licet mulierē versatili ingenio,variáque doctrina fuisse præditam.

EVANDER huius Nicostratæ, seu Carmentis, filius, cùm patrem imprudes interfecisset,relicta Archadia in Italiam venit,& pulsis Aborigenibus in Palatino monte cōsedit: agróque à Fauno iuniore Aborigenum Rege donatus, collem elegit,qui nunc in medio fermè vrbis est,in quo castellū seu oppidum extruxit,cui Pallantium,seu Pallanteū,nomen dedit, vel à Metropoli Archadię,vel de Pallantis proaui sui nomine circa annum mundi 2725. ante Christum natum 1237.paulò nempe ante quàm Hercules in Italiam ab Hispaniis aduentaret. Pallantium,Rom.postea Palatium dixere. Vide Diony.Halic.lib.1. & Cæli.Rhodi.lib.11.cap.17.& Vergi.lib.Enei.8.vbi sic inquit:

p.i: Archades his oris,genus à Pallante profectum, Qui Regem Euandrum comites,qui signa secuti, Delegere locum,& posuere in mentibus vrbem, Pallantis proaui de nomine,Pallanteum.

page.notes: The two medallions carry legends: "NICOSTRATA" on the left and "EVANDER" on the right, both engraved, not typeset text. Ligatures and the long-s forms were read as plain s. Greek and Hebrew: none on this page.
